proposedBellaRules.releaseScope: Already-agreed OMF1/Bento1 container/version/text/owner rules only; no OMF2, overlay, extended-label, Windows or raw-byte recovery support added.
proposedBellaRules.foundation: Validate complete supported TOC framing and required file-local mapping/membership/ownership before publishing that OMF contribution. One temporary TOC read/index followed by only needed metadata payloads; no whole media/essence read or permanent raw graph.
proposedBellaRules.valueFailure: Safely bounded bad text/numeric/payload/continuation invalidates that value and dependent answers; retain independent facts and only agreed separate fallbacks.
proposedBellaRules.linkFailure: Bad own ID, conflicting singular claim or unresolved required link invalidates dependent owner/association facts, not separately qualified branches. No arbitrary first/last or substitute unrelated owner.
proposedBellaRules.structuralFailure: Unsafe/incomplete shared framing or unusable required global ownership foundation rejects that OMF container contribution. Retain physical row and independent eligible database/filesystem/native-audio facts; expected format failures permit other files to continue. No unsafe structural-prefix salvage.
proposedBellaRules.completeness: Structural completeness differs from decoding every optional value. Relevant lookup must be complete to prove absence/default/NoReference; unrelated bounded optional failure does not prevent independent absence. Scope a bad mapping to demonstrably dependent facts when possible.
proposedBellaRules.unsupportedAndRepeated: Safely framed optional unknown data is skipped; needed unsupported forms unavailable. Preserve legitimate ordered arrays, declared continuations and identical repeats without treating all repetition as conflicting singular claims.
proposedBellaRules.fieldRules: Keep approved Unicode/separate legacy MacRoman, exact timing and damaged-vs-absent DF, Kind/Type/category, compression and summary rules. Short audio summaries omit samples intentionally; metadata readability is not media playback validation.
proposedBellaRules.sources: Native WAV/AIFF facts already independently read survive bad embedded OMF. No new fallback read, read trigger, priority or scheduling decision. General source capture/retry policy remains later; length stability is not proof against in-place change.
proposedBellaRules.implementation: Small C++17/Qt6.5.3 exact typed/bounds helpers, checked arithmetic/representability before indexing/allocation, scoped resources, compact availability/reasons and summary diagnostics. Release temporary bytes/indexes; no repair/recovery framework, permanent rejected-byte history or blanket corrupt catch.
proposedBellaRules.outcomes: Keep I/O, cancellation, detected source change, unsupported scope and resource/programming failures distinct from malformed metadata. Do not publish cancelled jobs as successful or hide out-of-memory/programming failures as corrupt files.
proposedBellaRules.noRepair: No automatic file/database delete, rewrite, rebuild, raw-byte resynchronization or guessed replacement records.
proposedBellaRules.currentBoundary: Current OMF metadata-only flow frames TOC before deferred payload reads; preserved partial source objects/no explicit framing gate is not proof of demonstrated decoded-prefix publication or crash. Broad Complete can inhibit independent absence/defaults.
proposedBellaRules.verificationBoundary: Static source/native checks and inspected synthetic cases; no malformed-input runtime campaign, damaged physical sample, native/private API/parser/test/build execution or measured Bella gain. No 100percent semantic/crash safety guarantee.

findings.claim: The generic OMFI open path has concrete false-return envelope failures, followed by a coarse success criterion, rather than detailed damaged-value/record/database statuses.
anchors: 0x100061cac..61ce8 rejects nil URL, nil whole-file NSData and fewer than 128 bytes.
0x100061d04..61d24 addresses the final 24-byte label and rejects magic different from raw a4434da5486472d7.
0x100061d3c..61dc4 dispatches Bento label major 2 to a log-only unsupported stub and returns false; other majors fall through to the flat reader without an explicit major-1 whitelist.
0x100061dc8..61dd8 rejects if the label recorded TOC byte length exceeds whole-file length.
0x100061e30..61e40 runs the flat reader and returns whether its counted objects are nonzero.
findings.limit: A true return is not proof that every required identity, property, list or value is valid. No actual corrupt input was executed.

findings.claim: The reviewed container code lacks several local geometry validations that Bella should provide instead of copying these pointer assumptions.
anchors: 0x100061e14..61e20 adds label TOC offset directly to file bytes. The preceding check compared TOC size alone to file size; no offset+size range check is present there.
OMFiTOCReader01 0x100061fe8..62000 divides recorded TOC byte length by 24 to obtain entry count. No nonzero/remainder/exact-24-byte-layout validation precedes that calculation.
howManyBentoObjectsV01 0x100061f64..61fb8 bounds its entry-count loop, but reads through the already constructed TOC pointer; it is not an independent TOC-range validator.
findings.limit: These are missing local checks in the bounded path, not a measured crash, exploit demonstration or complete format-support matrix.

findings.claim: pDataFor performs real pointer/length checks but does not constitute a fully checked typed property accessor.
anchors: 0x100061ebc..61ef8 returns nil for index -1, zero entry count, nil TOC/base pointers, index greater than count and zero recorded length.
The index test at 0x100061ed8..61edc uses count < index, so index equal to count is not rejected locally.
Flag word equal to 1 takes external storage: 0x100061f10..61f30 checks whole-file length >= uint32 offset + uint32 length using widened arithmetic, then returns base+offset.
For every flag other than 1, 0x100061f48..61f54 returns entry+12 as inline bytes without requiring the declared payload length to fit the four-byte immediate area or whitelisting other storage forms.
findings.limit: It does not validate declared property type, caller-specific minimum width, containment in a supported object region or ownership. No index/count malformed fixture was executed.

findings.claim: TOC lookup and counted reference iterations often skip nil/unresolved items, but local end/count validation is incomplete.
anchors: lookForProperty:At: 0x100063bb0..63bf0 scans until a property matches or object ID changes, returns 0 for absent property, and has no explicit entry-count/end-pointer bound in that method.
GetStringForObjectAt: likewise stops when the next entry object changes; its forward scan has no explicit entry-count bound.

OMFiTOCReader01 0x1000622ec..62498 uses pDataFor, skips nil or zero-count Composition/MediaData/Source mob indices, then reads 16-bit counts and advances 20-byte entries without validating count against that property length first.
0x100062254..622d4 decodes external dictionary-name bytes directly from entry offset/length, bypassing pDataFor range checks; failed ASCII conversion skips dictionary insertion.

getProjectAttributeForObjectAt: skips absent pointers, unresolved local references and nonmatching names; its 16-bit attribute count is not checked against recorded list length before the eight-byte reference loop.
findings.limit: Skip/continue cases do not prove arbitrary malformed lists are safe or that every broken reference invalidates only one field.

findings.claim: Generic row projection can keep other information when particular metadata is absent, but missing, damaged and unavailable are not cleanly separated.
anchors: addInfoToItem: 0x1000648bc..648c0 skips the master block if no master TOC was found; 0x100064aa8..64aac separately skips file-owned Project/format facts if no file TOC was found.

GetStringForObjectAt: 0x100063af4..63b44 returns nil for nil payload, zero length or failed Foundation decoding; it does not continue to another accepted string after the first selected property fails. The master setter stores that returned nil/empty value.
Master EditRate 0x100064944..64994 requires at least eight recorded bytes and a nonnil pDataFor pointer before loading its pair.
Master UsageCode 0x10006490c..64930 reads a 32-bit immediate TOC word without declared type/width/storage validation.
Project setter 0x100064ac8..64ad4 ignores nil Project, while nonnil empty Project overwrites prior text.

Compression helper has false-return missing descriptor/reference/required-compression paths and successful partial-result paths. Some scalar loads lack a caller-specific width check; DIDResolutionID path 0x100064cac..64cb4 does not test pDataFor return for nil before dereferencing it.
findings.limit: No general atomic record transaction, typed Missing-versus-Damaged result or universal per-value recovery policy is established. Do not claim nil alone proves correct damaged-field handling.

findings.claim: The ordinary scanner contains an Objective-C exception logging/continuation path, but this is not proven protection for all parser calls, C++ failures or hardware faults.
anchors: PMRScanner main landing path 0x10003a958..3a968 checks an exception selector then calls objc_begin_catch.
0x10003a98c..3aa2c logs Exception adding to foundClips and Item path; 0x10003aa48 ends catch and branches to row cleanup at 0x10003a944, which increments and continues the row loop.

No local catch handler is present in the fully inspected OMFI openFile, TOCReader01, pDataFor or property lookup bodies.
findings.limit: The language-specific exception table/protected call-site extent and exception type were not decoded here. Therefore the foundClips catch cannot be asserted to cover companion open, every OMFI decode or ordinary standalone OMF. ObjC catch calls do not establish recovery from invalid memory access, all C++ exceptions, allocation failure or corrupted state.

findings.claim: Generic reader wrappers carry a coarse open result, while standalone physical OMF inventory damage behavior remains unestablished.
anchors: MDVxMediafile openFile 0x100043af8..43b2c stores the reader result, reports false on failure and publishes its type only on success.
getMDBCompositionsCount wrapper 0x100043b58..43ba8 checks datasource, open-result byte and selector support, otherwise returns zero.
PMRScanner companion open at 0x10003a3a4 does not branch directly on the returned Boolean; its subsequent count wrapper observes the coarse result.
PMRScanner main 0x10003a8b4..3a8c0 uses companion MDB enrichment. The corresponding-file fallback helper 0x10003092c..30a14 gates physical opening on MXF.
findings.limit: No partial-container salvage, reparsing other versions, per-record continuation contract or crash-safety guarantee for standalone physical OMF can be inferred from generic browser extension dispatch.

smallestBellaLessons: Use the supported container envelope and checked offset/length arithmetic before creating byte views; reject metadata from a container whose TOC cannot be safely navigated.

Use one bounded typed property/list reader with exact scalar widths, supported storage flags, entry bounds, count-to-length checks and owner/reference qualification; do not reproduce blind pointer or first-match malformed-value assumptions.

Keep independent proven fields and the discovered physical row when a local optional value is unusable; stop dependent interpretation when required ownership/navigation facts cannot be trusted. Apply the already agreed per-field missing/damaged decisions instead of inferring one universal nil rule.
A compact read status and one file-level diagnostic summary are sufficient; no new recovery framework, crash-catching layer or salvage parser is supported by this comparison.
limits: Installed arm64 only; x86_64 not independently reconstructed.
Static local checks and absences are concrete; no malformed files, live exceptions, crash reproduction or reliability/performance measurement.
Do not claim all corruption is caught, all C++/ObjC failures are recoverable, every value failure preserves its row, or ordinary physical OMF fallback is proven.
No app/private API/media execution, repository edit, production parser/build/test or runtime cutover.

from pathlib import Path
import hashlib
import json
import subprocess

CACHE, VERIFIED, MISSING, EXCERPTS, CAPTURES = {}, {}, [], [], {}


def sha(path):
    p = Path(path)
    if str(p) not in CACHE:
        h = hashlib.sha256()
        with p.open('rb') as stream:
            for block in iter(lambda: stream.read(1024 * 1024), b''):
                h.update(block)
        CACHE[str(p)] = h.hexdigest()
    return CACHE[str(p)]


def record(path):
    p = Path(path)
    return {'path': str(p), 'bytes': p.stat().st_size, 'sha256': sha(p)}


def check(path, expected, context):
    p = Path(path)
    if not p.is_absolute():
        p = ROOT / p
    if not p.is_file():
        MISSING.append({'path': str(p), 'expectedSha256': expected, 'context': context})
        return
    assert sha(p) == expected, (context, str(p))
    VERIFIED[str(p)] = record(p)


def walk(value, context):
    if isinstance(value, dict):
        if all(k in value for k in ['path', 'startLine', 'endLine', 'sha256', 'text']):
            p = Path(value['path'])
            if not p.is_absolute():
                p = ROOT / p
            text = ''.join(p.read_text().splitlines(keepends=True)[value['startLine']-1:value['endLine']])
            assert text == value['text']
            assert hashlib.sha256(text.encode()).hexdigest() == value['sha256']
            EXCERPTS.append({'path': str(p), 'startLine': value['startLine'], 'endLine': value['endLine'], 'sha256': value['sha256']})
            return
        for pk, hk in [('path', 'sha256'), ('artifact', 'artifactSha256'),
                       ('resolvedArtifact', 'resolvedArtifactSha256'),
                       ('metadataSource', 'metadataSourceSha256'), ('classBlockPath', 'classBlockSha256')]:
            if isinstance(value.get(pk), str) and isinstance(value.get(hk), str):
                check(value[pk], value[hk], context)
        for key, child in value.items():
            walk(child, context + '/' + str(key))
    elif isinstance(value, list):
        for i, child in enumerate(value):
            walk(child, context + '/' + str(i))
